project.variant: V-Strom 650 ABS or ABS Adventure (DL650A): confirm from the VIN

INV-0033.name: Rear wheel, bearings and cush drive

A-001.title: Confirm which V-Strom you have
A-001.instructions: Read the VIN on the steering head and the frame label, check the model code and note whether it's the ABS or the ABS Adventure.
A-001.reason: The right manual and parts depend on the exact model.
A-001.expected: Model, year and VIN recorded in Settings.
A-001.inspectionCriteria: Model, year and VIN recorded in Settings.

A-002.title: Check for open recalls
A-002.instructions: Run the VIN through the NHTSA recall lookup and call a Suzuki dealer to confirm which recalls were done.
A-002.reason: 2012 bikes were covered by recalls for the stator, camshafts/tappets and the front brake light switch.
A-002.expected: Every recall marked done or booked with a dealer.
A-002.inspectionCriteria: Every recall marked done or booked with a dealer.

A-003.title: Get the service manual
A-003.instructions: Get the factory service manual for the 2012 DL650A and the owner's manual.
A-003.reason: Torque values, clearances and procedures in this course all come from the manual.
A-003.expected: Service manual on hand and listed under Reference sources.
A-003.inspectionCriteria: Service manual on hand and listed under Reference sources.

A-004.title: Set up the workspace
A-004.instructions: Clear a workspace with good light, a rear stand or lift, bins for fasteners, and a safe spot for fluids.
A-004.reason: A tidy space means fewer lost bolts and fewer accidents.
A-004.expected: Bike on a stand; labeled bins and drain pans ready.
A-004.inspectionCriteria: Bike on a stand; labeled bins and drain pans ready.

A-005.title: Set the budget
A-005.instructions: Set a budget in Settings with a cushion for surprises.
A-005.reason: Knowing the limit helps you decide between repair and replace.
A-005.expected: Budget and contingency set in Settings.
A-005.inspectionCriteria: Budget and contingency set in Settings.

B-001.title: Record the odometer and photograph the bike
B-001.instructions: Record the odometer, then photograph the bike from every side and close up on anything damaged.
B-001.reason: Before photos help at reassembly and record the condition you started with.

B-002.title: Check every fluid and look for leaks
B-002.instructions: Check engine oil, coolant, and front and rear brake fluid levels and condition, and look for leaks around the engine, radiator, forks and brakes.
B-002.reason: Low or dirty fluids and leaks point straight at the jobs you need to do.
B-002.expected: Each fluid level and condition recorded; leaks logged as problems.
B-002.inspectionCriteria: Each fluid level and condition recorded; leaks logged as problems.

B-003.title: Start it and listen
B-003.instructions: Start the engine, watch the warning lights, and listen for rattles, ticking or rough running as it warms up.
B-003.reason: Noises and warning lights at start-up are early warnings of bigger problems.
B-003.expected: Start-up behavior and warning lights recorded.
B-003.inspectionCriteria: Start-up behavior and warning lights recorded.

B-004.title: Short test ride, if it's safe
B-004.instructions: If brakes, tires and steering pass a basic check, ride slowly around the block and note how it brakes, shifts and handles.
B-004.reason: A ride shows problems you can't find on the stand.
B-004.expected: Ride notes written, or ride skipped with the reason recorded.
B-004.inspectionCriteria: Ride notes written, or ride skipped with the reason recorded.

B-005.title: Write the job list
B-005.instructions: Turn the inspection notes into a list of jobs, marking anything safety-related.
B-005.reason: A clear list keeps the project focused and drives the parts order.
B-005.expected: Problems logged with severity; job list agreed.
B-005.inspectionCriteria: Problems logged with severity; job list agreed.

C-001.title: Look up part numbers on the fiche
C-001.instructions: Use the factory parts diagrams for the 2012 DL650A to find the part number for everything on the job list.
C-001.reason: The right part number is the only reliable way to order the right part.
C-001.expected: Part numbers entered on each part in Parts.
C-001.inspectionCriteria: Part numbers entered on each part in Parts.

C-002.title: Price it and check the budget
C-002.instructions: Price each part from at least two shops including shipping and compare the total with the budget.
C-002.reason: Delivered prices vary more than you'd expect.
C-002.expected: Shopping list priced; budget forecast checked.
C-002.inspectionCriteria: Shopping list priced; budget forecast checked.

C-003.title: Order the parts
C-003.instructions: Order the parts and fluids, recording order dates and tracking.
C-003.reason: Ordering everything at once avoids stopping halfway through a job.

D-001.title: Remove the seat and side covers
D-001.instructions: Remove the seat with the key, then the side covers, bagging and labeling each fastener.
D-001.reason: Access to the battery, fuses and wiring starts here.
D-001.expected: Seat and side covers off; fasteners bagged and labeled.
D-001.inspectionCriteria: Seat and side covers off; fasteners bagged and labeled.

D-002.title: Remove the fairing and tank covers
D-002.instructions: Remove the tank covers, fairing side panels and any panels needed to reach the radiator and wiring.
D-002.reason: The cooling system and front wiring sit behind these panels.
D-002.expected: Panels off without broken tabs; all fasteners labeled.
D-002.inspectionCriteria: Panels off without broken tabs; all fasteners labeled.

D-003.title: Disconnect the battery
D-003.instructions: Disconnect the battery, negative first, and remove it for testing and charging.
D-003.reason: Working with the battery connected risks shorts and damage to the ECU and ABS unit.
D-003.expected: Battery out and on a smart charger.
D-003.inspectionCriteria: Battery out and on a smart charger.

E-001.title: Wash and degrease
E-001.instructions: Clean the bike so you can see the frame, engine and wiring, protecting electrical parts and intakes.
E-001.reason: You can't inspect what you can't see.
E-001.expected: Bike clean; no water in connectors or intakes.
E-001.inspectionCriteria: Bike clean; no water in connectors or intakes.

E-002.title: Inspect the frame, subframe and swingarm
E-002.instructions: Inspect the frame, subframe, footpeg mounts and swingarm for cracks, bends and crash damage.
E-002.reason: Crash damage on the frame or subframe makes the bike unsafe.
E-002.expected: Frame and subframe checked; any damage logged.
E-002.inspectionCriteria: Frame and subframe checked; any damage logged.

E-003.title: Inspect wiring and connectors
E-003.instructions: Look over the harness for rubbed insulation, melted spots and green corrosion in connectors.
E-003.reason: Chafed wires and corroded connectors cause intermittent faults that are hard to find later.

F-001.title: Test and charge the battery
F-001.instructions: Fully charge the battery and test it under load or with a battery tester.
F-001.reason: Every other electrical test is meaningless with a weak battery.

F-002.title: Inspect the stator and regulator connectors
F-002.instructions: Inspect the connector between the stator and the regulator/rectifier and the regulator's mounting and wiring.
F-002.reason: A burnt connector here is a common sign of charging trouble, and the stator is under recall on these bikes.

F-003.title: Test the charging system
F-003.instructions: With a good battery fitted, measure charging voltage at the battery and test stator output using the manual's procedure.
F-003.reason: This confirms the stator and regulator are doing their job.
F-003.expected: Readings recorded and compared to the manual's figures.
F-003.inspectionCriteria: Readings recorded and compared to the manual's figures.

F-004.title: Check grounds, lights, switches and warning lamps
F-004.instructions: Clean the main ground points, then test every light, the horn, switches and the warning lamps including ABS.
F-004.reason: Riders need to see and be seen. The brake light switch on 2012 bikes was under recall.
F-004.expected: Every light and switch works; brake light works from lever and pedal.
F-004.inspectionCriteria: Every light and switch works; brake light works from lever and pedal.

G-001.title: Drain and refill the coolant
G-001.instructions: Drain the coolant on a cold engine, flush if needed, and refill with the type the manual specifies, bleeding out the air.
G-001.reason: The schedule calls for new coolant every four years.
G-001.expected: System full, bled, and the reserve at the right level.
G-001.inspectionCriteria: System full, bled, and the reserve at the right level.

G-002.title: Inspect the radiator, hoses and cap
G-002.instructions: Check the radiator for leaks and blocked fins, and the hoses and clamps for cracks, swelling or seepage.
G-002.reason: Radiator hoses are on a four-year replace schedule.
G-002.expected: Radiator and hoses checked; replacements ordered if due.
G-002.inspectionCriteria: Radiator and hoses checked; replacements ordered if due.

G-003.title: Confirm the fan works
G-003.instructions: Let the engine reach temperature at idle and confirm the fan switches on and off.
G-003.reason: A dead fan means overheating in traffic.
G-003.expected: Fan switches on at temperature and off again.
G-003.inspectionCriteria: Fan switches on at temperature and off again.

H-001.title: Replace or clean the air filter
H-001.instructions: Remove the air filter, inspect it, and replace it if it's due or dirty.
H-001.reason: A clogged filter costs power and fuel economy.
H-001.expected: Clean or new filter fitted; intake checked for debris.
H-001.inspectionCriteria: Clean or new filter fitted; intake checked for debris.

H-002.title: Inspect the fuel lines and clamps
H-002.instructions: Inspect the fuel lines and clamps for cracks, hardening and seepage.
H-002.reason: Fuel lines are on a four-year replace schedule, and a fuel leak is a fire risk.
H-002.expected: Fuel lines checked; replaced if due.
H-002.inspectionCriteria: Fuel lines checked; replaced if due.

H-003.title: Clean the throttle bodies and set cable play
H-003.instructions: Clean carbon from the throttle plates and set the throttle cable free play to the manual's figure.
H-003.reason: Sticky plates and wrong cable play cause a jerky throttle.
H-003.expected: Plates clean; cable play within spec; throttle snaps shut.
H-003.inspectionCriteria: Plates clean; cable play within spec; throttle snaps shut.

H-004.title: Synchronize the throttle bodies
H-004.instructions: Synchronize the two throttle bodies with a vacuum gauge set, following the manual's procedure.
H-004.reason: Out-of-sync throttle bodies make the bike lumpy at low speed.
H-004.expected: Both cylinders balanced per the manual.
H-004.inspectionCriteria: Both cylinders balanced per the manual.

I-001.title: Change the oil and filter
I-001.instructions: Drain the warm oil, replace the filter and drain bolt washer, and refill with the oil the manual specifies.
I-001.reason: Fresh oil is the cheapest engine protection there is.
I-001.tools: Drain pan, filter wrench, torque wrench
I-001.expected: New oil and filter; level correct in the window; no leaks.
I-001.inspectionCriteria: New oil and filter; level correct in the window; no leaks.

I-002.title: Replace the spark plugs
I-002.instructions: Replace all four spark plugs (two per cylinder) with the type the manual lists.
I-002.reason: The schedule replaces plugs at 7,500 miles.
I-002.expected: Four new plugs fitted to the correct torque.
I-002.inspectionCriteria: Four new plugs fitted to the correct torque.

I-003.title: Set the clutch cable play
I-003.instructions: Set clutch cable free play at the lever with the adjuster.
I-003.reason: Too little play makes the clutch slip; too much makes shifting hard.
I-003.expected: Free play within the manual's range.
I-003.inspectionCriteria: Free play within the manual's range.

I-004.title: Check the valve clearances (when due)
I-004.instructions: If the bike is at or past the valve-check interval, or the cam recall applies, measure the valve clearances cold and adjust per the manual.
I-004.reason: The schedule calls for a check at 14,500 miles, and 2012 to 2014 bikes had a cam and tappet recall.
I-004.expected: Clearances recorded in Measurements and within spec.
I-004.inspectionCriteria: Clearances recorded in Measurements and within spec.

J-001.title: Check tire age, tread and damage
J-001.instructions: Read the date code on both tires, measure the tread, look for cracks, plugs and flat spots, and set the pressure.
J-001.reason: Tires age out even with tread left.
J-001.expected: Both tires pass or replacements ordered.
J-001.inspectionCriteria: Both tires pass or replacements ordered.

J-002.title: Check the wheel bearings
J-002.instructions: With each wheel off the ground, check for play and rough rotation.
J-002.reason: Worn bearings make the bike wander and can fail.

J-003.title: Check the chain, sprockets and cush drive
J-003.instructions: Measure chain wear and slack, inspect sprocket teeth and check the rear cush drive rubbers.
J-003.reason: A worn chain can jump or break.
J-003.expected: Chain and sprockets pass or a kit is ordered; slack set to the manual's figure.
J-003.inspectionCriteria: Chain and sprockets pass or a kit is ordered; slack set to the manual's figure.

K-001.title: Inspect pads and discs
K-001.instructions: Check pad thickness and disc thickness, scoring and warping on both brakes.
K-001.reason: Worn pads and thin discs are a straight safety issue.
K-001.expected: Pads and discs within limits or replacements ordered.
K-001.inspectionCriteria: Pads and discs within limits or replacements ordered.

K-002.title: Clean the calipers and fit pads
K-002.instructions: Clean the calipers and pistons, check the pistons move freely, and fit new pads if needed.
K-002.reason: Sticky pistons cause dragging and uneven braking.
K-002.expected: Pistons move smoothly; pads fitted correctly.
K-002.inspectionCriteria: Pistons move smoothly; pads fitted correctly.

K-003.title: Replace the brake fluid (ABS)
K-003.instructions: Replace the front and rear brake fluid with the type on the reservoir cap, following the manual's ABS procedure.
K-003.reason: The schedule replaces brake fluid every two years.
K-003.expected: Fresh fluid, firm lever and pedal, no leaks.
K-003.inspectionCriteria: Fresh fluid, firm lever and pedal, no leaks.

K-004.title: Inspect the brake hoses
K-004.instructions: Inspect the brake hoses for cracks, bulges and leaks.
K-004.reason: Brake hoses are on a four-year replace schedule.
K-004.expected: Hoses checked; replacements ordered if due.
K-004.inspectionCriteria: Hoses checked; replacements ordered if due.

L-001.title: Check the forks
L-001.instructions: Look for oil on the fork tubes, pitting on the chrome, and check damping. Replace the oil and seals if they're leaking or due.
L-001.reason: Leaking seals let oil onto the brakes and worn oil makes the front dive.
L-001.expected: Forks dry and damping smooth, or service done.
L-001.inspectionCriteria: Forks dry and damping smooth, or service done.

L-002.title: Check the steering head bearings
L-002.instructions: With the front wheel off the ground, check for notchiness and play, and adjust or replace the bearings.
L-002.reason: Worn steering bearings make the bike weave and feel vague.

L-003.title: Check the rear shock and linkage
L-003.instructions: Check the shock for leaks, the linkage for play, and grease the linkage bearings.
L-003.reason: Dry linkage bearings wear fast and make the rear end clunk.
L-003.expected: Shock dry, linkage greased, no play.
L-003.inspectionCriteria: Shock dry, linkage greased, no play.

L-004.title: Set the sag, preload and rebound
L-004.instructions: Measure sag with you on the bike and set rear preload and rebound for your weight and load.
L-004.reason: The right sag makes the bike handle the way it was designed.

M-001.title: Refit the bodywork
M-001.instructions: Refit the panels in reverse order using the labeled fasteners.
M-001.reason: Correct fasteners keep panels quiet and mounts intact.
M-001.expected: Every panel fitted; no leftover screws.
M-001.inspectionCriteria: Every panel fitted; no leftover screws.

M-002.title: Torque-check the critical fasteners
M-002.instructions: Check axles, pinch bolts, caliper bolts, handlebar clamps and the drain bolt against the manual's torque values.
M-002.reason: These are the fasteners that keep the wheels and brakes on.

M-003.title: Test ride and recheck
M-003.instructions: Ride carefully, test brakes and ABS at low speed, then recheck for leaks, fluid levels and loose parts.
M-003.reason: The first ride is where small mistakes show up.
M-003.expected: Ride notes recorded; nothing leaking or loose.
M-003.inspectionCriteria: Ride notes recorded; nothing leaking or loose.

N-001.title: Set up the maintenance schedule
N-001.instructions: Open the Maintenance log, check the schedule items against your owner's manual, and set when each was last done.
N-001.reason: The log can only tell you what's due once it knows when things were done.
N-001.expected: Every schedule item has a start point.
N-001.inspectionCriteria: Every schedule item has a start point.

N-002.title: Log the work you just did
N-002.instructions: Log a service record for the work in this project with parts, cost and receipts.
N-002.reason: A complete history adds value and makes the next service easy.
N-002.expected: Service logged with parts and receipts.
N-002.inspectionCriteria: Service logged with parts and receipts.

N-003.title: Back up the project
N-003.reason: Your records are worth keeping somewhere safe.

LAB-0001.work: Pulled the side covers and fairing panels, labeled every fastener.

LAB-0002.work: Checked the stator connector and grounds. Connector was browned, ordered a new one.

ISS-0001.description: Stator recall (NHTSA 16V878000): 2012-2016 DL650 stators could overheat and short, which can stall the engine.
ISS-0001.proposed: Check the VIN on nhtsa.gov/recalls. If open, a Suzuki dealer replaces the stator for free.

ISS-0002.description: Camshaft and tappet recall (NHTSA 15V852000) for 2012-2014 DL650A.
ISS-0002.proposed: Ask a Suzuki dealer whether it's been done for this VIN. Check valve clearances if unsure.

ISS-0003.description: Front brake light switch recall (12V038000) listed for the 2012 DL650A.
ISS-0003.proposed: Confirm by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and with a dealer. Test the brake light from the front lever.
ISS-0003.notes: Found on an aggregator only (au7o.io). Confirm with NHTSA by VIN.

GATE-01.name: Bike identified and recalls checked
GATE-01.criteria: Model, VIN and recall status recorded.

GATE-02.name: Condition recorded and job list agreed
GATE-02.criteria: Before photos, fluid checks and the job list are in the app.

GATE-03.name: Electrical and charging pass
GATE-03.criteria: Battery, charging readings and lights all pass.

GATE-04.name: Cooling, fuel and air done
GATE-04.criteria: Coolant, hoses, filter, lines and sync done or recorded as not needed.

GATE-05.name: Engine service done
GATE-05.criteria: Oil, filter, plugs and clutch play done.

GATE-06.name: Wheels, tires, chain and brakes pass
GATE-06.criteria: All in limits with fresh brake fluid.

GATE-07.name: Suspension and steering pass
GATE-07.criteria: No leaks, no steering play, linkage greased.

GATE-08.name: Road test passed
GATE-08.criteria: Fasteners checked, ride done, recheck clean.

SAFE-001.criteria: NHTSA lookup shows no open recalls, or dealer work booked in writing.

SAFE-002.criteria: Axles, pinch bolts, caliper bolts and bar clamps checked to the manual's values and marked.

SAFE-003.criteria: Firm lever, no leaks, pads and discs in limits.

SAFE-004.criteria: Firm pedal, no leaks, pad and disc in limits.

SAFE-005.criteria: Light on with the key, off once moving.

SAFE-006.check: Tires in date, tread and pressure
SAFE-006.criteria: Date codes recorded, tread above the legal minimum, pressures set.
